stage1.impression: A symmetrical timber niche with two speakers on plinths, lit from two downlights, seen across a large, empty, near-black floor. At 1:1 the fir reads as clean veneer with no checks or nail holes. The plinth tops have a white LED-like edge glow, the white batts read as flat white boxes, and a tan card floats in front of the right plinth. It reads as a showroom render of a hi-fi alcove, not a photograph of a lived-in listening bar. As it stands a magazine would see a generic hi-fi showroom, not a specific place: the shell (concrete, beams, steel), the chairs and the Orbs that would make it Planet EARF are all out of frame or lost in black.

blocking_9: The listening zone (velvet tub chairs, oak tables, lit Orbs) must be in frame and legible between the camera and the altar, so the frame shows a room for listening and not an empty floor
The shell (board-formed concrete with tie holes, Douglas fir beams, blackened steel) must be visible in at least one side or the ceiling plane, so the place is specific
The plinths' top-edge glow must read as light falling on oak, not as an LED strip or signage
The fir lining must show real timber detail at 1:1 (checks, darker end grain, board-to-board variation), not uniform veneer
Visible haze or atmosphere in the spot cones, and light pools on the floor, so the darkness has depth
Every prop must sit believably on a surface (no floating tan card at the right plinth)

defects.what: A quarter of the frame is a flat, featureless dark floor (median 23.8, range 32.9): no rug, no furniture, no pools of light. It reads as empty.
The left edge is near-black void (median 12.7). The shell and the counter side of the room are lost.
Blurred, cut-off foreground objects (an Orb and a glass?) are unreadable fragments at the frame edge.
A white glowing rim along the plinth top reads as an LED strip (p95 244, clip 0.18%).
The same white LED-like rim on the right plinth.
A flat tan rectangle (the sleeve against the plinth) reads as a floating card with no shadow or contact.
The white batts read as flat white blocks pasted inside the cabinet, brighter than everything around them.
Horn reflections are smeared, wobbly blobs, not clean reflections of the room.
The Douglas fir reads as uniform, regular veneer: no checks, nail holes or end grain, and the boards repeat.
Two hotspots on the lining's top edge from the altar spots, with the speakers' fronts lit flat beneath them.
No visible haze; the spot cones have no volume; fine grain or noise over the shadows.

changes.problem: The frame shows an empty floor and the shell is lost, so it reads as a generic hi-fi showroom, not the listening zone of a specific bar.

evidence.measured: floor median 23.8 with range 32.9 (featureless); left edge median 12.7; the chairs and Orbs only appear as cut-off blurs at the bottom left

change.to: pull back to about x 10.8, seated height z 1.05, off-axis at y 4.2, target about [16.6, 2.9, 1.0], 32 mm, so that two tub chairs with an oak table and a lit Orb fill the lower third in front of the altar and a strip of side shell (concrete or a fir beam) shows at one edge

changes.expected: The lower third holds chairs, a table and an Orb pool instead of black floor. The altar stays the hero in the upper middle. The room reads as a place to sit and listen.

changes.problem: The plinth tops glow as white LED strips, which reads as signage or a display case.

evidence.measured: p95 244.3, clip 0.18% on the plinth rim; the same on the right plinth

change.setting: on each speaker 4 x area (the speaker's lamps) / altar spots
change.to: 0.2 W/m2 at 2700 K, and let the altar spots at a 24 deg cone light the plinths' oak faces instead

changes.expected: The plinth tops read as lit oak with a soft gradient and no white line; the plinths' fronts show grain.

changes.problem: The altar spots make two hotspots on the lining's top edge and light the speakers flat from above, not as a pool on the pair.

evidence.measured: falloff along y 138 -> 97 -> 68 -> 47 then back up to 77; the brightest band is the lining's top edge, not the speakers

change.to: 45 W, 2500 K, cone 24 deg, aimed at the speakers' horn and upper cabinet (about 1.0 m above the plinth top) rather than the lining's top

changes.expected: The brightest pool sits on the speakers and the fir falls off above them. The speakers read at a glance.

changes.problem: The shadows are void, with no pools on the floor, so the room is dim but not cozy or readable.

change.setting: the Orbs (power and liner glow), plus the Domes' downlights
change.from: each Orb 0.058 W, glow 0.0092; downlights 80 W
change.to: each Orb 0.15 W, glow 0.02, so each table gets a warm pool; downlights 80 W kept; add 2 votives on the zone's tables

changes.expected: Warm pools on the tables and chairs between the camera and the altar, with dark between them; the shadow side holds detail.

changes.problem: No atmosphere: the spot cones have no volume and the depth reads flat.

evidence.measured: no visible beam in the cones under the soffit; median 42.7

changes.expected: Faint cones under the altar spots and a little veil in the dark, as in a real bar at night.

changes.problem: The sleeve against the right plinth reads as a flat tan card floating in front of the plinth.

evidence.measured: flat patch, range 34.3, median 68.2, no contact shadow

change.setting: props: the sleeve against a plinth
change.from: upright, square to the camera, in front of the plinth's face
change.to: leaned at about 15 deg against the plinth's side, touching the floor, with a record half out of it, and a second sleeve on the nearest tub table

changes.expected: The sleeve sits on the floor with a contact shadow and reads as a record sleeve.

changes.problem: The Douglas fir lining reads as uniform CG veneer at 1:1.

evidence.measured: seen at 2x: regular boards, identical grain, no checks or nail holes

change.to: per-board tone variation of about +/-10%, fine checks, occasional nail holes, a slightly raised grain with roughness 0.55, a faint oil sheen

changes.expected: The lining reads as old-growth fir boards, warm and slightly irregular.

changes.problem: The whites of the batts and the horn's reflections are the brightest neutral things in the frame and pull against the warm room.

evidence.measured: speaker region p95 226; the batts read near white beside a fir median of r106/g67/b40

change.to: AgX - Medium Contrast, exposure 4.6, with a highlight roll-off so the batts sit near lum 180 and the horn reflections soften

changes.expected: The batts read as soft white inside the smoked acrylic, not as pasted blocks; the frame's median stays in range.

out_of_scope.request: Make the horns' reflections cleaner by changing their surface
out_of_scope.why: The horn is part of EARF's speaker, which is fixed; only the light and the environment it reflects may change.

out_of_scope.request: Add colour so the speaker is the saturated hero
out_of_scope.why: Smoke is the house configuration, and the speakers' tint is fixed; the speaker can only become the hero through light and composition.

out_of_scope.request: Bring board-formed concrete or beams into the niche itself
out_of_scope.why: The niche's fir lining is the room's design as proposed; the shell can only enter by moving the camera (c1).
